english.html: And as to Carbon Barrau, uncle of the said du Tilh, and other witnesses who particularise so closely the facts against the said prisoner, they have been sharply and validly objected to, and the objections found good and well proved. The saying of the soldier counts for nothing either: for he has not been heard, but it is others who depose that they heard him say it.

Inasmuch as a witness ought to depose of what he can perceive and comprehend by one of his bodily senses, and not of what he has heard from another a. The testimony of having heard another say something, although it makes some sort of presumption b, nevertheless is not sufficient to make proof c; unless it were to show kinship or affinity, to the end of preventing some marriage d — and then, provided that such testimony be accompanied by rumour and common repute, together with other adminicles [supporting proofs] and circumstances e2; or else to make appear some very old and ancient fact f, as to prove the very ancient limits and bounds of one's lands g. And what is said above must be soundly understood of the testimony of having heard a third party say it; for as to having heard one of the parties pleading say it, the testimony would be very good h: as to have heard that Antoine promised a hundred écus to Pierre, which Pierre now demands of him; or else to have heard that Lucrece has espoused Camille by words of the present, and now this marriage between Camille and Lucrece is in question i.

notes.citation: Code 4.20 (De testibus), l. Testium (law not identified); Decretum, C. 22 q. 5, c. Hoc videtur (chapter number unverified)
notes.original: l. teſtium C. de teſtib. c. hoc videtur. xxij. q. v.
notes.gloss: A witness is to speak to what he has himself perceived.

notes.citation: The Archdeacon (Archidiaconus, Guido de Baysio) on the c. Hoc videtur cited before (C. 22 q. 5)
notes.original: Archiadia. de auc. hoc videtur. pre allegue.⟨alt:allegué.⟩
notes.gloss: The print's Archiadia. de auc. is read as Archidia. au c. Hearsay raises some presumption though it proves nothing.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Licet ex quadam (cf. X 2.20.47), cited before
notes.gloss: Innocent III admits hearsay of kinship, with common repute, in a matrimonial cause to prove an impediment.

notes.citation: Decretals X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Praeterea (chapter not identified); Panormitanus (Panorme) on c. Licet ex quadam, cited
notes.original: c. præterea. de teſt. Panor me au c. licet ex quadam. allegue.
notes.gloss: Hearsay of kinship is received only when accompanied by common repute and other adminicles. On the key e2, see the headnote: it should read e once annot-052's marker is corrected.

notes.citation: Digest 22.3 (De probationibus et praesumptionibus), l. Si arbiter (cf. D. 22.3.28, Labeo; number unverified)
notes.original: l. ſi arbitrer. D. de probatio.
notes.gloss: Ancient facts beyond living memory may be proved by what has been heard from the old.

notes.citation: Baldus (Balde) on Code 1.3 (De episcopis et clericis), l. Conventicula (law not identified)
notes.original: Balde en la l. conuenticulam. C. de. epiſ. & cler.
notes.gloss: Hearsay admitted to prove the ancient bounds of lands.

notes.citation: Accursius (Accurse) on Digest 39.3 (De aqua et aquae pluviae arcendae), l. 2, § Idem Labeo (D. 39.3.2; paragraph unverified); the Gloss on Decretum, C. 22 q. 5, c. Hoc videtur (as note a)
notes.original: Accurſe en la l ij. P. Idem Labeo. D. de aq. pluu. Glo ſe au c. hoc vi detur. xxij. q v.
notes.gloss: What a witness heard a party himself say is good testimony, being the party's own admission.

notes.citation: The Doctors on Digest 22.3, l. Si arbiter (as note f) and on Decretals X 2.20, c. Tam litteris (as note c), cited above
notes.original: Les Docteurs en la l. ſi arbitrer & au c. tam literis. deſſus alleguez.
notes.gloss: The examples of the promise overheard and the espousals overheard.
